observations: The page number «228» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it; at the left the number of the table, «Tab. 113», in bold sans serif, underlined. The page has no signature and no title: the folios of the manuscripts stand at the left above the double rule of the first field, in one line of their own, «C 101v, O 157r. N 68r.», the letters raised, with a point after «157r»: see the critical note (L01).

The page holds three fields, as pp. 206-227 (JP2 0238-0259): «Quinque1) gradus Piscium2)» (L02), «Decem6) gradus Piscium» (L14) and «Quindecim7) gradus Piscium» (L22), the ascendant at 5°, 10° and 15° of Pisces, with the numbers for the sextile, the quadrature and the trine (L03, L15, L23); headings and numbers in bold. The notes 3, 4 and 5 stand after the three numbers of the first field: O omits them. The columns begin with the sign of the ascendant: «Pisces Virgo Horoscopus», «Aries Libra Horoscopus», «Taurus Scorpius Horoscopus», «Gemini Sagittar. Horoscopus», «Cancer Capricorn. Horoscopus» and «Leo Aquarius Horoscopus», without notes; here each head is set from the top, one printed line to a line (L04-L06), with «Gradus aequales», printed upwards, in L04-L05, and the units in L07. The numbers are counted from the beginning of Pisces. The paired note a stands at the first number of the first column of the first field (L08) and at the last of the third (L29): C omits the first column of all three fields; it is set «a)-a)», with a short stroke of 10 px at the foot of the line between the letters, where the other paired notes of these tables have a dash. The second and the third field have no heads. Double rules divide the fields.

The numbers at the head of a field, as on pp. 206-227 (JP2 0238-0259), are a third, a half and two thirds of the last number of the field. The second and the third field end with the same number, 145° 55′ (L21, L29), and have the same heads, 48° 38′, 72° 58′ and 97° 17′ (L15, L23), the third, the half and the two thirds of 145° 55′ being 48° 38.3′, 72° 57.5′ and 97° 16.7′; in the second the quadrature is N's 58 (note e: C and O 38). In the first field the sextile 48° 19′ and the trine 96° 39′ (L03) are a third and two thirds of its last number, 144° 58′ (L13), whose half is 72° 29′; the quadrature has 74° 29′, from C (note 4: O omits the head).

Suter's third example (p. 101, JP2 0133, L21-L27) uses the first field: the ascendant at 5° of Pisces, the planet at 25° of Cancer. The column of Cancer has 117° 13′ at 25° (L12), and with the sextile 48° 19′ (L03) the sum is 165° 32′, more than the last number of the field, 144° 58′ (L13); the remainder, 20° 34′, falls between 18° 30′ at the end of Virgo and 21° 15′ at 5° of Libra (L13, L08), and the interpolation gives 3° 45.5′ of Libra for the left sextile, Suter's 3° 45′. Suter's numbers 117° 13′, 165° 32′, 144° 58′ and 20° 34′ are those of the table. That a sum larger than the last number of a field is diminished by it, and its place sought again in the same field, agrees with the rule of the heads: the last number of a field answers to a semicircle, 180°, of which the sextile, the quadrature and the trine, 60°, 90° and 120°, are a third, a half and two thirds; the columns then serve for the opposite signs named under the first (Virgo under Pisces, Libra under Aries).

The columns: in Pisces and Aries the three fields lie within 9′, 10′ and 10′ of the oblique ascensions from the beginning of Pisces for the latitude 38° 30′ (computed with the obliquity 23° 35′; 3° 15′, 6° 24′, 9° 30′, 12° 32′, 15° 33′, 18° 32′ in Pisces), except in Aries in the first field, which lies 5′ to 18′ below them; from Taurus on they rise above them, by up to 3° 15′, 3° 17′ and 2° 42′ about the end of Gemini and the beginning of Cancer, then fall below them from 25° of Cancer in the first and the third field and from 30° of Cancer in the second, and end 16° 20′, 15° 23′ and 15° 23′ below them (144° 58′, 145° 55′ and 145° 55′ for 161° 18′ at the end of Leo). The first field lies 2′ to 30′ below the second in Aries, Taurus and Cancer; in Leo the second and the third agree within 10′ but at 5° of Leo (below).

Notes on the readings. Checked by the rule of the heads, by the other fields, which differ by 5° of the ascendant, by the oblique ascensions and by the steps of the columns: the edition's readings are the nearer at 25° of Aries in the first field (note b, L12: O's 33 against C's 34, the steps 3° 15′ and 3° 20′ against 4° 15′ and 2° 20′), at 20° of Taurus and 30° of Cancer in the first (notes c and d, L11, L13: C's 52 against O's 2; C's 122 against O's 120, the steps 5° 5′ and 4° 0′ against 3° 5′ and 6° 0′), in the quadrature of the second (note e, L15: N's 58, above), at 15° of Pisces in the second (note f, L18: C's 30 against O's 20; 9° 30′ is the oblique ascension, and the steps are 3° 10′ and 3° 0′ against 3° 0′ and 3° 10′, those of the oblique ascensions 3° 6′ and 3° 2′), at 15° of Aries in the second (note g, L18: the 27 of O and N against C's 28, the steps 3° 0′ and 3° 15′ against 4° 0′ and 2° 15′), at 15° of Cancer in the second (note i, L18: the editor's 107 for the 106 of C and O, the steps 5° 20′ and 5° 0′ against 4° 20′ and 6° 0′), at 5° and 20° of Pisces in the third (notes m and l, L24, L27: the editor's 15 for C's 5 and O's 9, 3° 15′ being the oblique ascension of the first 5° of Pisces and the steps 3° 15′ and 3° 15′; C's 12 against O's 11, the steps 3° 7′ and 2° 56′ against 2° 7′ and 3° 56′) and at 30° of Taurus in the third (note n, L29: the 60 of O and N against C's 55, less than the 55° 35′ before it). At 10° of Taurus in the second field (note h, L17) O's 30, C's 25 and N's 35 give the steps 3° 35′ and 4° 10′, 3° 30′ and 4° 15′, 3° 40′ and 4° 5′; at 25° of Leo in the second (note k, L20) C's 20, the number of the third field at the same place (L28), gives the steps 3° 31′ and 3° 35′, O's 15 3° 26′ and 3° 40′; neither is decided. Note a: C omits the first column.

Without variants: in the second field 126° 15′ at 5° of Leo (L16) lies 25′ below the third field (126° 40′), where the two fields agree within 10′ in the rest of Leo, between the steps 3° 35′ and 4° 37′; with 126° 45′ they would be 4° 5′ and 4° 7′. In the third field the column of Taurus rises unevenly, by 3° 30′, 4° 0′, 4° 10′, 3° 10′, 3° 50′ and 4° 40′ (L24-L29).

A point stands after the 15 of the first column in L10, after the 101 of Cancer in L25 and before the 30 of Cancer in L19, and a point at mid-height between the sign of the degrees and the 58 of the quadrature in L23; specks, not transcribed. Italics: «om.».
